learner_operation: Recognize u=ax+b, determine the slope a, scale the numerator n by 1/a, and select (n/a)ln|ax+b|+C while distinguishing coefficient and argument errors.

fixed_features.feature: One affine denominator, one constant numerator, one indefinite integral.
fixed_features.justification: Canonical e-449 and the general-formula tutorial teach one reciprocal substitution; combinations belong to adjacent KPs.

fixed_features.feature: Five math radio choices with exactly one answer.
fixed_features.justification: All six captured practice banks use this response contract.

fixed_features.feature: New bank options share the slope and have positive numerator candidates.
fixed_features.justification: All source numerators are positive. Keeping easy integer numerators and a common slope does not fix the correct candidate: all five bank candidates become targets. Determining n/a remains necessary. Signed slope still varies.

answer_roles.role: Correct coefficient sign, magnitude and rank
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Both slope signs; unit/nonunit slopes; each eligible coefficient rank may be correct.
answer_roles.observed: All five keys occur for identical banks in the target batch and both controlled profiles; positive and negative slopes occur in the regression sample.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Preserve the affine argument matching the integrand; allow either argument group in a mixed bank to supply the answer.
answer_roles.observed: Target batch has 2 choices with 8x+4 and 3 with 8x+6; each becomes correct. Controlled mixed bank likewise varies its qualifying argument.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Radio position is incidental and should not predict the answer.
answer_roles.observed: Generator and actual UI shuffle positions; both controlled templates have distinct displayed correct positions.

coverage.case: Zero intercept with positive unit slope
coverage.result: Invalid x0 notation in this supported decision case; math/rendering fail independently of varied answer-role assignments.

counterfactuals.change: Hold each five-choice bank fixed; vary the numerator and, in the mixed template, the intercept that supplies the integrand.
counterfactuals.expected: The keyed antiderivative must track the selected n/a and argument; prompt and worked substitution must change with the target.
counterfactuals.observed: Five distinct prompts, solutions and correct values per bank; all choices independently differentiated and exercised in the native grader. Rendered coefficient and argument changes match.
counterfactuals.justification: Canonical substitution and source shifted-argument distractors make both coefficient and argument relevant.

counterfactuals.change: Hold parameters and full bank fixed; change only the seeded option order.
counterfactuals.expected: Preserve prompt, solution and correct mathematical value; grading must accept that value at its new position.
counterfactuals.observed: Both profiles preserve all three dependencies, change choice order, and pass native correct/wrong-choice tests. Both rendered before/after pairs inspected.
counterfactuals.justification: Radio option order is absent from the source integration rule.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose the largest coefficient; break ties by lexical argument, without consulting the prompt.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is uniform choice among five options. Successes are bounded sample measurements, not a universal probability claim. stages_examined: within-band learner selection and history subsets
delivery.result: The five runner records survive and have five different keys in a shared bank; old shortcut no longer solves them. Fresh controls retain coverage. Dedup removes two irrelevant reorder duplicates from controlled pairs. All five malformed seed-575 records also survive, so separate math failure remains deliverable.

limitations: Finite probes do not prove absence of every shortcut.
The current batch supplies only one mixed-argument bank; it supports practice on five different numerator/argument decisions, not independent coverage of every slope sign.
Math and notation validity fail at a=1,b=0; pedagogical key-variation success does not waive this defect.
Selection conclusions are conditional on captured inventory and supplied code; no live learner policy/history is available.
